present: A cop writing a parking ticket
A beautiful woman in a red dress
summary: Morpheus leads Neo through a crowded downtown street where Neo is bumped and shouldered while Morpheus explains that the Matrix is a system that is their enemy and that the people inside it are still part of it. When Morpheus catches Neo distracted by a woman in a red dress, he says 'Look again' and Neo turns to find Agent Smith leveling a gun at his face, making Neo scream. Morpheus freezes everything except the two of them and reveals this is another training program, explaining that Agents are sentient programs who can move in and out of any software hardwired to the system, meaning anyone not unplugged is potentially an Agent. Morpheus says they are the gatekeepers guarding all doors and that every man or woman who fought an Agent has died, but Neo will succeed because their strength and speed are based on a world built by rules. When Neo asks if he can dodge bullets, Morpheus says 'when you're ready, you won't have to.' Morpheus' cell phone rings and Tank announces 'We got trouble.'

what_changes.before: Believes he is walking through the Matrix itself, confused about what he is seeing.
what_changes.after: Learns he is in a training program and that Agents are sentient programs who can be anyone not yet unplugged.
what_changes.evidence: This -- this isn't the Matrix? No, it's another training program designed to teach you one thing

what_changes.before: A man being told about enemies in the abstract, distracted enough to notice a woman in a red dress.
what_changes.after: A man who has screamed at a gun to his face and learned he is expected to fight Agents that have killed everyone before him.
what_changes.evidence: Neo turns just as Agent Smith levels a gun at his face. Neo screams.

what_changes.before: Assumes Agents are simply unbeatable, asking if he must dodge bullets.
what_changes.after: Learns Agents' strength and speed are bound by rules, so he can become stronger and faster than them.
what_changes.evidence: their strength and their speed are still based on a world that is built by rules. Because of that they will never be as strong or as fast as you can be.

event_hint.one_line: Morpheus trains Neo inside a simulation, teaching him what Agents are and that he can surpass them, until Tank interrupts with news of trouble.

objects_that_matter: the woman in the red dress

minds.wants: To understand what he's walking through and to prove—mostly to himself—that he belongs in this fight.
minds.feels: Disoriented and overmatched. The crowd physically buffets him, the Cop's stare unsettles him, and the sudden gun-to-face jolt leaves him raw; underneath the fear is a thread of relief that this is a program, not reality, because reality would mean he's already dead twice.
minds.shows: Confusion, a flustered evasion about the woman in the red dress, a scream he can't suppress, then a defensive, almost jokey skepticism ('Are you trying to tell me that I can dodge bullets?') that masks how badly the gun got to him.
minds.basis: Neo is 'constantly bumped and shouldered' and struggling to keep up; he's caught staring at the woman and stammers; he screams when the gun appears; he scratches his head and reframes Morpheus's lesson as a comic superhero claim.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is testing whether he's paying attention, and that the whole thing is a lecture he can coast through.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus isn't checking attention—he's demonstrating that inattention gets you killed; the woman was bait and the gun was the lesson.

believes_about.belief: That the Agent is an unbeatable force, so the only survivable move is to become fast enough to dodge bullets.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus corrects him directly: the real advantage isn't dodging, it's that the Agent is bound by rules Neo can learn to rewrite.

minds.wants: To install in Neo, experientially rather than abstractly, exactly what he's up against—and to do it without breaking his nerve.
minds.feels: Under pressure he does not show: this is the part of training where a candidate can panic and quit, and Morpheus is betting everything (see the Oracle debate in sc-064) on this man. He stages fear deliberately, then withdraws it the instant it's served its purpose.
minds.shows: Total calm. He lets the crowd jostle Neo, catches the distraction without anger, freezes the terror he engineered, and delivers the deadliest facts ('everyone who fought an Agent has died') in the same steady register he used for the sidewalk lecture—then pivots to 'you will succeed.'
minds.basis: He engineers the red-dress→gun sequence on purpose ('Look again'), freezes it on a dime, and follows the death sentence with an immediate promise of victory grounded in rules. He withholds the comforting reveal until the fear has landed.

believes_about.belief: That Neo can be taken to the edge of terror and back without shattering—that the scream is the beginning of learning, not the sign of a lost cause.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is faith, not yet fact; it's the same conviction Cypher mocks in sc-064, and the event-shape (five prior candidates who died) means Morpheus could be wrong about this one too.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is ready to hear that Agents can be anyone unplugged—the paranoia lesson—without it making him distrust the very people they're trying to save.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus can't know whether 'everyone is potentially an Agent' teaches caution or teaches contempt; Neo has no frame yet to hold the distinction.

minds.wants: Nothing active in this scene—she is not present—but her presence is the quiet pressure behind Morpheus's stakes.
minds.feels: Not legible here; any reading would be invention.
minds.basis: Trinity is not in sc-065. The only trace is indirect: Morpheus's determination to make Neo succeed is the same conviction she defended in sc-064 ('when he's ready'), but she herself does not act or react in this scene.

connects_back: sc-062: Neo's 'I thought it wasn't real' / 'your mind makes it real' is the premise Morpheus exploits here—the gun feels lethal because Neo's mind believes it, yet Morpheus now reveals even that terror was a controlled simulation.

sc-064: Cypher's 'why doesn't he take him to the Oracle' and Trinity's 'when he's ready' establish that Neo's success is an article of faith Morpheus is defending—this scene is Morpheus investing in that faith.
ev-013: After the rooftop fall proved Neo still doubts, this is the next rung—replacing fear-of-failure with knowledge of the enemy.
sets_up: ev-016 restates this exact street/Agent lesson, so Neo's 'everyone is potentially an Agent' knowledge becomes the baseline he operates on when they later move through the real Matrix.
ev-018 (Cypher's warning that five prior candidates died fighting Agents) is the counter-argument to Morpheus's 'you will succeed' planted here—the two claims are now in direct collision.
Morpheus's 'when you're ready, you won't have to [dodge bullets]' sets the ceiling Neo's training is aimed at, making later feats of surpassing the rules believable rather than abrupt.
Tank's 'We got trouble' interrupt ends the classroom safety and pushes the crew from training into the mission that ev-017 (hiding from the Sentinel) and beyond will demand.
dramatic_function: It converts the abstract enemy into a felt, personal threat and then immediately hands Neo a reason to believe he can win—staging fear and withdrawing it—so that the audience and Neo accept both the lethality of Agents and the plausibility of the One surpassing them, all under the shadow of Morpheus's embattled faith.
